title: Shut down the company
summary: Close the company through its jurisdiction’s approved dissolution or liquidation route, settle obligations, complete final tax filings, withdraw remaining registrations and retain the records.

parts.title: Draft the required corporate dissolution approvals
parts.guidance: Prepare the dissolution approvals with counsel using ownership, liabilities, assets and the proposed closure route. Address employees, creditors, contracts, taxes and records in the plan. Identify filings triggered by adoption, including Form 966 where applicable, and calendar them before signatures. Resolve the company’s eligibility for the proposed route and the decision-makers required to authorize it.

execution.rationale: Draft dissolution approvals and a filing checklist from counsel-settled closure instructions and supplied company records.

parts.title: Sign the corporate dissolution approvals
parts.guidance: Obtain the approvals required for the chosen dissolution route from the actual directors, stockholders or other decision-makers. Present the final plan and financial consequences, then check voting requirements, capacities and document consistency. Record the true adoption date and notify the closure coordinator, because filings may run from that event. Resolve incomplete approvals before relying on the plan as authorized.

execution.rationale: Required company decision-makers review and personally sign the dissolution approvals through the agreed digital corporate process.

parts.title: Run the final payroll and terminate contractors
parts.guidance: Resolve final compensation, notices, benefits, contractor invoices, equipment and access for each departing person and location. HR, payroll and counsel handle the relevant local requirements. The responsible company representatives authorize termination communications and payments. Reconcile completed payments and outstanding claims, and retain the staff access needed to finish payroll reporting, tax work and closure.

execution.rationale: The shutdown owner coordinates final payroll and contractor termination digitally and accounts for the physical return of company equipment included in the departure work.

parts.title: Cancel vendor contracts and subscriptions
parts.guidance: Review contracts and subscriptions for termination rights, notice methods, final charges and data exports. Include services holding records needed after closure. Send authorized cancellation notices, retain acknowledgements and verify billing stops. Export necessary records before accounts disappear, and keep essential communications and storage running until their custodians can complete dependent closure work.

execution.rationale: The responsible owner cancels vendor contracts through their account or correspondence channels, exports required records and verifies billing and retention consequences.

parts.title: Submit the dissolution or closure filing and settle registry obligations
parts.guidance: Use the closure route approved for this entity and jurisdiction. Reconcile corporate approvals, creditor and registry requirements, and any outstanding charges before the authorized person approves filing and payment. Retain acceptance evidence and follow the local winding-up sequence.

options.title: United States — Delaware dissolution forms
options.summary: Select the appropriate Delaware dissolution certificate and confirm the corporate approvals supporting it. Reconcile annual-report and franchise-tax requirements for the corporation ending its existence. The authorized officer approves the certificate, timing and payments before submission. Keep the accepted filing and continue the separate work on claims, taxes, distributions and records.

verify.how: The Delaware entity search shows the corporation's status as dissolved once the certificate is stamped.

cost.note: Certificate of Dissolution (§275) filing fee; franchise taxes must be brought current to dissolve, and the §391 short form is $50 where eligible.

execution.rationale: Use the signed-paper Delaware dissolution filing route where applicable, including the required personal execution and delivery after tax clearance.

options.title: India - STK-2 strike-off or IBC liquidation
options.summary: Review the Indian company’s activity, liabilities, assets and filing status with a local professional to determine the available closure route. Assess strike-off or formal liquidation against current requirements before choosing either. Establish the necessary approvals, creditor treatment and tax work, then carry out authorized filings through the local process. The subsequent US forms do not constitute an Indian closure procedure.

execution.rationale: Counsel and the authorized owner administer the selected closure procedure through digital case, filing and creditor records; the legal route remains a professional decision.

options.title: UK - DS01 voluntary strike-off
options.summary: Check voluntary strike-off eligibility against the company’s trading, creditor, asset and insolvency position. Resolve required communications and remaining assets and obligations before the authorized directors approve applying. Follow Companies House notices through the actual outcome. If the company is ineligible, assess the appropriate alternative closure route.
options.when: Winding up in the United Kingdom

execution.rationale: Required directors personally approve the closure and an authorized filer completes the supported digital strike-off and follow-up process.

options.title: Germany - liquidation + Sperrjahr
options.summary: Confirm the German dissolution decision, liquidators, registry filings and creditor process with local counsel. Assess assets and liabilities and the distribution restrictions in GmbHG section 73 before authorizing payouts. Track liquidation separately from final register removal, keeping the required corporate and registry evidence. Use the local sequence and applicable German tax filings for subsequent closure work.

execution.rationale: The liquidator and advisers coordinate the required decisions, creditor notices, filings and distributions through the digital closure record and applicable services.

options.title: France - dissolution then radiation
options.summary: Assess whether voluntary dissolution fits the French company’s financial and ownership facts. Follow the appropriate dissolution decision, liquidator’s work, closure accounts and radiation process, with associated tax and social filings identified separately. Obtain the required approvals for submissions and distributions and retain decisions and registry evidence. The local closure sequence governs follow-up, including which tax forms apply.

execution.rationale: Authorized company representatives and advisers manage the dissolution and registration closure through the applicable digital filing and notice services.

geoResolutions.label: Delaware dissolution forms
geoResolutions.guidance: Wind down and dissolve the corporation: board and stockholder dissolution consents, the final payroll and contractor terminations, vendor cancellations, final tax returns with IRS account closure, the Delaware certificate of dissolution with franchise-tax true-up, state withdrawals, bank closure with final distributions, and records retention. Select the appropriate Delaware dissolution certificate and confirm the corporate approvals supporting it. Reconcile annual-report and franchise-tax requirements for the corporation ending its existence. The authorized officer approves the certificate, timing and payments before submission. Keep the accepted filing and continue the separate work on claims, taxes, distributions and records.

geoResolutions.label: Wind-down runs through the registry's dissolution-and-liquidation channel (the encerrar-o-negócio guide maps it), plus the final Modelo 22 and IES and the cessação de atividade declarations to the tax authority and Segurança Social.

A solvent corporation dissolves by shareholder-authorized articles of dissolution filed with Corporations Canada; the certificate of dissolution ends the final tax year, so the final T2 (due within six months of that year end) and the CRA program-account closures (payroll, GST/HST) follow the certificate.

When the company closes down you ask the Companies Office to remove it from the register, after working through the before-you-close steps; a company that ignores its Companies Act 1993 obligations can be removed by the Registrar instead.

A solvent exit is an ACRA strike-off application through Bizfile — the process runs at least 2 months after approval, with gazette notices — or a members' voluntary winding up for larger balance sheets; clear the IRAS filings first.

A solvent company whose members all agree, with assets under $1,000 and no outstanding liabilities, applies for voluntary deregistration with ASIC (Corporations Act 2001 s 601AA); bigger balance sheets run a members' voluntary liquidation. Cancel the GST/PAYG registrations and the ABN and lodge the final company tax return with the ATO.

Winding down runs on two tracks: dissolution and liquidation registrations with the court registry (IROS), and business-closure reporting to the tax office through Hometax, with the final VAT return due within 25 days after the closure month.

A solvent exit is deregistration: obtain the Commissioner of Inland Revenue's Notice of No Objection, then apply to the Companies Registry, with gazette notices before the company dissolves — a members' voluntary winding up is the heavier route for larger balance sheets.

Winding down runs through the commercial register: the shareholders resolve dissolution, liquidation is entered and run, and the company is deleted after creditor protection, with tax deregistration through e-MTA alongside.

parts.title: Wait for the dissolution to be accepted
parts.guidance: Follow the registry’s acceptance or correction requests and verify the effective dissolution date against the filing. Resolve discrepancies with the filer or counsel and save the accepted record. Continue the applicable tax, creditor and records work under the closure plan. Registry acceptance is one milestone within winding up; it does not establish that remaining obligations are finished.

execution.rationale: The responsible owner monitors the dissolution filing and answers the registry's requests through its correspondence channel, retaining the accepted result when issued.

parts.title: Your accountant prepares the final tax returns
parts.guidance: Give the accountant the final books, asset dispositions, payroll, contractor payments, prior returns and closure approvals. Identify the returns, periods, final-return designations and related forms for this entity and jurisdiction, with each deadline tracked independently. Resolve open accounting items before return review.

geoResolutions.label: The CPA prepares the final federal and state returns, each marked final
The final Modelo 22 and IES close out the entity's tax years
The certificate of dissolution ends the final tax year, so the final T2 is due within six months of that year end

execution.rationale: The accountant prepares final returns from digital closure records and coordinates outstanding tax issues and signature responsibilities with the company.

parts.title: Sign the final tax returns and closure declarations the jurisdiction requires
parts.guidance: Have the authorized person review and sign the final tax returns, filing authorizations and closure declarations required for the entity. Use the forms and sequence confirmed by the local adviser.

execution.rationale: Use the signed-paper route for required final jurats and Form 966; the responsible signatory completes execution while the accountant tracks each filing requirement.

geoResolutions.label: Sign the final return jurats and Form 966
geoResolutions.guidance: Review final returns and any required Form 966 against the closure records, then obtain the proper human signature or electronic authorization. Check Form 966’s separate deadline from adoption of the dissolution or liquidation plan; it may precede final-return preparation. Keep required resolution attachments with the filing and resolve factual discrepancies before submission.

parts.title: File the final returns and close the tax accounts
parts.guidance: Authorize the reviewed final tax filings and check acknowledgements and payments. Reconcile outstanding obligations before requesting closure of the entity's tax accounts under current instructions. Keep the tax identifier in historical records as the entity’s permanent identifier. Assign a reachable person to later notices, and track actual account-closure status separately from the company’s dissolution filing.

geoResolutions.label: Close the IRS business account once federal obligations reconcile; the EIN stays on record as the entity's permanent identifier

verify.how: The final returns are marked final and the IRS closing-a-business checklist is completed for the EIN account.

geoResolutions.label: File the cessação de atividade declarations to the tax authority and Segurança Social
Close the CRA program accounts (payroll, GST/HST) after the certificate of dissolution

execution.rationale: The accountant and authorized filer complete final-return authorization, submission, payment and account closure through the relevant digital services.

verify.how: Retain the applicable authority’s confirmation and reconcile it with the approved submission and company records.

parts.title: Withdraw registrations outside the home jurisdiction
parts.guidance: Check every foreign-state registration for its withdrawal procedure and outstanding reports, taxes or clearances. Submit the approved withdrawal and fee, then follow it through acceptance. Keep agent coverage where still required during closure and update the jurisdiction record when withdrawal is confirmed. A home-state dissolution does not automatically terminate registrations elsewhere.

verify.how: Each state's business search shows the registration withdrawn or terminated.

execution.rationale: The company or filing adviser coordinates foreign-state withdrawals through the applicable filing services, retaining separate approvals and acceptance records.

parts.title: Close bank accounts and distribute remaining assets
parts.guidance: Reconcile cash with remaining debts, taxes, fees and contingent claims. Counsel and the financial adviser determine appropriate reserves and distributions under the winding-up plan. Authorized company representatives approve transfers to verified recipients. Close accounts only after remaining payment and receipt needs are resolved, and preserve the final statements and distribution evidence for the custodian.

execution.rationale: Mercury documents transferring remaining balances, checking pending transactions, downloading final records and requesting closure in its dashboard. Reconcile those records against the adviser-approved winding-up plan before distributing funds. The beneficial owner must authorize and complete the restricted closure request; counsel and finance determine reserves and recipients.

parts.title: Archive corporate records for retention
parts.guidance: Preserve corporate decisions, ownership, contracts, employment, tax and financial records with the closure evidence. Apply the relevant retention requirements and legal holds. Name a reachable custodian and test access to storage that will survive closed subscriptions and employee accounts. Arrange where future notices will arrive and who can retrieve documents or address unresolved matters.

execution.rationale: The records owner archives the company documents in the selected digital store and verifies continuing ownership, access and notice delivery after closure.

metadata.supportReason: The agent drafts the consents, runs the final payroll, cancels vendors, and prepares every filing; the dissolution consents and return jurats need real signatures, and the Delaware, IRS, and bank-closure steps are portal or mail work.

geoNotes.summary: Two exits: MCA strike-off via form STK-2 for a company with no liabilities, or a formal voluntary liquidation under the IBC run by an insolvency professional and overseen by the IBBI — both slower and more document-heavy than a US dissolution.

A solvent company applies for voluntary strike-off with a £33 DS01 filing to Companies House (or a members' voluntary liquidation for larger balance sheets) — closer to one filing than the DE dissolution + IRS final-return chain.

Winding up a GmbH is slow by design: a notarized dissolution resolution, liquidators registered, creditors publicly invited — then a mandatory one-year Sperrjahr before assets can distribute and the company is finally deleted from the Handelsregister.

The sequence is dissolution (shareholder decision + legal-announcement publication), a liquidation phase closing the accounts, then radiation from the RCS — every step filed through the guichet unique.
